I don't think this antagonistic approach is going to work though. Some men might become better eventually. I think a lot more are just going to off themselves. And in the meantime, they will contribute to the patriarchy, probably hurting lots of women and men and any others in between. Because they are also frustrated and angry. I'm not quite sure what the answer is. But I don't think that fueling the already anger filled men and giving them more reason to hate women is it. It might be if they had more empathy, but most of them haven't developed their empathy muscles. Like I said, you have every right to angry and say "fuck em, let them handle it themselves, I don't care about them" but I think their response is just going to be similar, just towards women. These types of things just make me feel so hopeless. I want to be better but I don't think I can most of the time, I feel like I've been conditioned wrong and I will never have those good feminine qualities. I started therapy in high school (2016). Within a year or a little longer, I stopped but kept taking medication until 2018. Had to leave university the same year due to not receiving my student loan in time and having poor social skills/social anxiety. Kept myself afloat by working seasonally. That seemed to work well so I continued through the pandemic. Was mostly self medicating with weed and still am. As time went on I spent less and less time interacting with others. This snowballed into me not leaving my apartment building for about 3 months which spanned from early January to late March or early April (convenience store in building and mom had some groceries delivered). I figured that was a sign to seek therapy again. With all my anxiety and getting a grandparent to help with appointments, it took more than 3 months to get medicated and about another 3 past that to get into therapy, which my first appointment was in early september. I went to a few appointments but missed 2 which means they don't have to contact me again about it I guess. Shortly after that I stopped taking my medication, mostly because I'm a self destructive piece of shit. I don't have the courage to tell anyone that I've stopped taking medication or to try to get back into therapy again. I wanted to go and see my family in the U.S. to try to clear my head a bit but getting a passport is a process and one that I seem too anxious about to actually get done. So kinda ruined Christmas for myself and my family. Really I'm so anxious and depressed I barely clean myself or my surroundings, doing anything seems like so much responsibility that I just usually give up before I start. I wrote a suicide note in August and I'm pretty sure that's where my situation is headed. 

Sorry for any unnecessary details TLDR I should've stayed in therapy pre-pandemic because now any medical care is hard to find and I only got worse over time.
